security: Native prb_commit/prb_final_commit publish/release the reservation; no borrowed writer-buffer ownership remains after them. Capture data before commit and expose a synchronous snapshot after commit. This preserves hook order/timing/signatures and valid observation data, but intentionally removes the ability to mutate the already committed record through r. Such raw mutation is incompatible with the LTS ownership protocol. The noinline enabled-hook helper uses 1024 bytes of bounded text storage plus metadata on the stack; disabled hooks do not allocate that snapshot frame. Recursion remains native (PRINTK_MAX_RECURSION=3), but total worst-case nested IRQ/NMI stack use is not runtime verified. Native ringbuffer, nbcon and printk_safe files are exact LTS. Formatting arrays are initialized and terminated; this bounds ordinary %s consumption, not malicious out-of-bounds writes by trusted modules. Hotplug skip and caller attribution remain explicit vendor policy freedoms.
uncertainty: No definite printk/logbuf hook registrations found in scoped GrapheneOS system/device-generic or manifest common-modules source searches. Retain generic configured module interfaces conservatively. External callbacks depending on illegal post-commit raw-buffer mutation need adaptation to the documented observation snapshot contract; current SDK callbacks and runtime timing are unverified.
validation: Extracted host helpers/functions pass 1024 commit/reuse cases and 3900 formatting cases; ACK controls produce 5776 and 2580 failing assertions respectively. Commit observer overwrites source storage immediately before hooks; no actual ringbuffer/concurrency is executed. Build 115 succeeded at 4e85d32c517a: both kernel images, 100 common and 45 virtual-device modules, 145 cryptographically verified signatures and protected-export/module-table checks. Actual enabled-hook helper prologue is recorded in evidence/printk-stack-build-115.json.
